nodes.label: A-30 Single tenant (AM-14)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-30 single tenant (am-14)
nodes.rationale: Single tenant (AMPM only); no organisation_id column anywhere. AMPM confirmed: for AMPM's internal use, not for licensing. If AMPM intends to license the software, add organisation_id to every root table before build; it is expensive to retrofit.

nodes.label: A-26 Function status versus readiness (AM-3)
nodes.norm_label: a-26 function status versus readiness (am-3)
nodes.rationale: functions.status (planned, confirmed, cancelled) and functions.readiness_status are two fields; readiness is derived from the function's checklist. AMPM confirmed the readiness rule; the two fields stand. Could merge into one field if AMPM prefers.

nodes.label: A-27 Room category capacity (AM-5)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-27 room category capacity (am-5)
nodes.rationale: hotel_room_categories.room_count is the inventory in that category; max_occupancy is per room. Not addressed by AMPM; stands.

nodes.label: A-28 Demo data isolation (AM-8)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-28 demo data isolation (am-8)
nodes.rationale: Default: demo data lives in the same database, isolated by client_accounts.is_demo, wedding_projects.is_demo and hotels.demo_visible; demo accounts see a curated subset of real hotels with rate items masked and one sample project. AMPM changed: demo shows up to three locations and one or two sample hotels each with indicative prices and street view, after OTP; limits and duration configurable and to be finalised. A separate demo database would remove the flags and add a copy job.

nodes.label: A-29 Subscription scope (AM-9)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-29 subscription scope (am-9)
nodes.rationale: A subscription belongs to an account and covers every project on that account. Not addressed by AMPM; stands. Per-wedding subscriptions would add subscriptions.project_id.

nodes.label: A-1 Platform form factor (Q1)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-1 platform form factor (q1)
nodes.rationale: Default: responsive web application with one backend for team workspace, client portal and guest portal; no native apps in v1; Phase 4 adds installable PWA mode with read-only offline caching of run-of-show and checklists. AMPM 2026-10-25 changed: native iOS and Android apps with offline use from launch; the web remains for the public website; whether the client portal also needs a web version is open. Schema impact: native apps change nothing except adding a device_tokens table for push notifications; the offline change queue is a client-side store mirrored by audit_events on sync.

nodes.label: A-10 Phase 1 scope (Q10)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-10 phase 1 scope (q10)
nodes.rationale: Default: Phase 1 includes demo/trial, the full ten-status hotel enquiry flow, online payment and a minimal built-in CMS; phase tags per table in §19. AMPM changed: first release includes discovery, wedding management, vendors, client portal, department access, RSVP, requests, live chat and offline operations; excludes website editing, online milestone payments and GST invoicing; single or staged launch to be agreed.

nodes.label: A-11 Notification channels (Q11)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-11 notification channels (q11)
nodes.rationale: Default: in-app, email and WhatsApp (via a business service provider) with SMS fallback, enumerated in notifications.channel. AMPM partly decided: email and WhatsApp required, SMS proposed, providers to be confirmed; live chat added. Unused channels are disabled in configuration.

nodes.label: A-12 Built-in CMS (Q12)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-12 built-in cms (q12)
nodes.rationale: Default: minimal built-in CMS (cms_pages, cms_showcase_items) for destinations, showcase items and page copy. AMPM dropped it: no website editing in the app; the website is maintained outside the platform. A headless CMS would replace the two tables with an integration.

nodes.label: A-13 Authentication (Q13)
nodes.norm_label: a-13 authentication (q13)
nodes.rationale: Default: clients sign in with email and password, phone OTP optional second factor; staff must use email, password and an authenticator app (TOTP); guests use token links only and never have accounts. AMPM changed: prospects, demo users and clients sign in with mobile number and OTP; staff method to be finalised (authenticator recommended). Phone-OTP-only makes users.password_hash nullable and adds an OTP flow on auth_tokens.

nodes.label: A-14 Hosting (Q14)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-14 hosting (q14)
nodes.rationale: Default: hosted in an Indian region with private object storage; no schema impact, noted so retention and residency rules are consistent. AMPM still open: hosting to be confirmed with the developer.

nodes.label: A-15 Sizing (Q15)
nodes.norm_label: a-15 sizing (q15)
nodes.rationale: Default sizing for index and partition choices: up to 50 staff users, 40 concurrent projects, 1,500 guests per project, 500 hotels, 2 TB of media in year one. AMPM changed: about 200 hotels and 20 concurrent weddings; staff and guest capacity to be confirmed. Larger volumes change indexing and partitioning (audit_events, notifications, guest_function_attendance), not the model.

nodes.label: A-16 Currency, GST, language, time zone (Q16)
nodes.norm_label: a-16 currency, gst, language, time zone (q16)
nodes.rationale: Default: single currency INR with a currency column wherever money appears; GST fields on invoices and invoice lines; English only; time zone per project, default Asia/Kolkata. AMPM confirmed INR and English; the platform does not issue GST invoices, so GST fields are dormant. Multi-currency would add exchange-rate snapshots on payments and budget_lines.

nodes.label: A-17 Retention (Q17)
nodes.norm_label: a-17 retention (q17)
nodes.rationale: Default retention classes: closed leads 24 months; guest personal data 12 months after project close; identity documents checkout plus 30 days; demo data reset on a schedule; retention_class and retention_until on documents and identity_documents, client_access_until on wedding_projects. AMPM changed: no automatic deletion; retention and deletion require AMPM approval; periods to be confirmed; jobs become proposed deletion lists awaiting approval.

nodes.label: A-18 Several hotels and venues per wedding (Q18)
nodes.norm_label: a-18 several hotels and venues per wedding (q18)
nodes.rationale: Default: a wedding may use several hotels (project_hotels) and venues outside the database (external_venues); wedding_projects.primary_hotel_id is a convenience pointer only. AMPM confirmed multiple hotels and venues per wedding.

nodes.label: A-19 Room blocks and allocations (Q19)
nodes.norm_label: a-19 room blocks and allocations (q19)
nodes.rationale: Default: room blocks held per project, hotel, room category and date range; allocations reference a block; occupants are individual guests, children included; sharing rules not enforced by the schema. AMPM confirmed: room blocks by hotel, category and dates; team-managed allocation; room-wise and person-wise counts, children included. Rules such as two adults per room become validations.

nodes.label: A-2 Payment path (Q2)
nodes.norm_label: a-2 payment path (q2)
nodes.rationale: Default: Phase 1 supports both an online gateway (webhook-driven activation) and offline payment recorded manually by Finance; both create a payments row; subscription activation keys off payments.status = succeeded. AMPM changed: online payment only, by card or UPI, after AMPM creates or invites the account and the client enters basic wedding details; gateway to be selected; manual recording stays as a staff fallback. Offline-only would leave provider/provider_ref unused; online-only disables method = bank_transfer.

nodes.label: A-20 Chat versus tracked questions (Q20)
nodes.norm_label: a-20 chat versus tracked questions (q20)
nodes.rationale: Default: no free-form chat in v1; a client question is a client_requests row of type question with a threaded comments trail, logged and visible to the assigned team. AMPM changed: live chat is required in addition to tracked requests, adding conversations and messages.

nodes.label: A-21 Change requests (Q21)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-21 change requests (q21)
nodes.rationale: Default: change requests are client_requests of type change_request with the §11 statuses; a configurable threshold marks a request is_material. AMPM confirmed, with a closed status added. A separate table only if the workflow diverges from questions.

nodes.label: A-22 No vendor or hotel logins (Q22)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-22 no vendor or hotel logins (q22)
nodes.rationale: Default: vendors and hotels never log in; users.user_type has no vendor value. AMPM confirmed. A vendor portal later adds a vendor user type scoped to vendor_assignments; vendors unchanged.

nodes.label: A-23 Post-closure client access (Q23)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-23 post-closure client access (q23)
nodes.rationale: Default: clients keep read-only portal access for 12 months after closure (wedding_projects.client_access_until), then the project is archived. AMPM changed: three months of read-only access, then archiving on AMPM approval. The period is configuration.

nodes.label: A-24 Feedback and archive (Q24)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-24 feedback and archive (q24)
nodes.rationale: Default: post-wedding feedback is a client_feedback row; archive is wedding_projects.archived_at plus retention jobs. AMPM confirmed feedback form and archived state.

nodes.label: A-25 Material change thresholds (Q25)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-25 material change thresholds (q25)
nodes.rationale: Default: a change is material when it exceeds configurable thresholds (e.g. a budget line delta of 10 percent or a date or venue change); material changes set is_material and populate impact_flags_json, which drives the SPEC §8 automation. AMPM partly decided: configurable thresholds confirmed; values and approval rules to be defined.

nodes.label: A-3 Plans, trial and demo (Q3)
nodes.norm_label: a-3 plans, trial and demo (q3)
nodes.rationale: Default: plans supports one-time fixed-term and recurring billing; v1 configured one-time fixed-term with manual renewal; trial is subscription status trial on a plan with trial_days; demo is a plan flagged is_demo on an account flagged is_demo; entitlements come from plan_modules. AMPM confirmed: Rs 50,000, one-time, one month, configurable; renewal is a new purchase; no separate trial plan, the demo serves that purpose. Recurring billing would need subscription_invoices and dunning states; auto_renew and ends_at already exist.

nodes.label: A-4 Margin and client-facing amounts (Q4)
nodes.norm_label: a-4 margin and client-facing amounts (q4)
nodes.rationale: Default: AMPM may earn a margin on vendor and hotel pricing, so every commercial record stores client-facing amounts and internal cost in separate columns (vendor_proposals, hotel_proposals, budget_lines, room_blocks, project_final_accounts). Clients see estimates, approved amounts, invoices issued to them, their own payments and outstanding milestones; never vendor quotes, internal cost, margin, vendor invoices or vendor contracts. AMPM partly decided: internal cost and margin never shown confirmed; wedding management fee set outside the app; online milestone payment out of the first release; which client-facing amounts the portal shows still to be confirmed. A transparent fee model would need no structural change.

nodes.label: A-5 Client users per wedding (Q5)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-5 client users per wedding (q5)
nodes.rationale: Default: several client users per wedding through project_members with project_role client_owner / client_approver / client_viewer; can_view_finance flag; approvals need one decision by default, approvals.required_decisions allows more. AMPM changed: two family representatives, one per side, with equal rights; no viewer role and no finance flag; shared or separate logins to be decided, separate recommended.

nodes.label: A-6 Roles and cost visibility (Q6)
nodes.norm_label: a-6 roles and cost visibility (q6)
nodes.rationale: Default: the eleven SPEC §6 roles adopted as global staff roles plus external roles (client via project membership, guest via token, demo prospect). Internal cost and margin readable by Super Admin and Finance everywhere, the Wedding Project Manager on assigned projects, the Vendor Coordinator for vendor-side cost and the Hotel team for hotel-side cost. AMPM partly decided: department-based access confirmed; final role list and who may see hotel and vendor costs to be confirmed. Role changes alter roles and role_permissions seed data only.

nodes.label: A-7 Guest list and RSVP model (Q7)
nodes.norm_label: a-7 guest list and rsvp model (q7)
nodes.rationale: Default: guest list loaded first (client upload or AMPM entry); each family group receives a unique tokenised RSVP link; guests respond per person per function; a group may add accompanying members up to family_groups.max_additional_guests (default 0); no open registration; dietary preference for everyone, allergies and accessibility optional and SENSITIVE; client sees own guest list except RESTRICTED and identity fields. AMPM changed: links per side or one combined link (final structure open); guests identify themselves against the loaded list; no editing after submission; corrections through the RSVP team; per-person counting, meal preference and allergies confirmed; family representatives see summaries only and cannot edit the list. A shared wedding link needs self-identification and a de-duplication queue, with rsvp_tokens.family_group_id nullable.

nodes.label: A-8 Identity documents (Q8)
nodes.community_name: Data Model Assumptions and Public Content
nodes.norm_label: a-8 identity documents (q8)
nodes.rationale: Default: collected only when a project enables it for a defined purpose (hotel check-in); Aadhaar numbers never stored; accepted passport, voter ID, driving licence; files in a separate restricted bucket; retention_until defaults to checkout plus 30 days; every read audited. AMPM partly decided: per wedding, no Aadhaar and restricted storage confirmed; automatic deletion removed; retention follows AMPM-approved policy, to be confirmed. If Aadhaar is legally needed, add document_type = aadhaar_masked after legal review.

nodes.label: A-9 Hotel commercials and availability (Q9)
nodes.norm_label: a-9 hotel commercials and availability (q9)
nodes.rationale: Default: indicative rate cards with line items (room rate by category, venue rental, per-plate minimums, taxes), client-visible once verified; negotiated rates in hotel_proposals with client and internal amounts; availability checked manually per enquiry, no calendar; per-asset media rights; hotels bulk-imported through import_jobs. AMPM confirmed and extended: prices are indicative ranges including wedding package ranges and per-plate pricing, menu grids, street view; Eva updates about three times a year; about 200 hotels at the start. A live calendar would add hotel_availability_days.

nodes.label: Changes from AMPM's decisions of 25 October 2026 (§0a)
nodes.norm_label: changes from ampm's decisions of 25 october 2026 (§0a)
nodes.rationale: Decisions that changed the model: Q9 indicative price ranges, wedding packages, street view; Q2 couple_names and preferred_locations at activation; Q5 two family representatives; Q7 RSVP link scope, self-identification, locked responses, correction requests; Q20 live chat module Q; Q8/Q17 no automatic deletion; Q23 three-month access window and archived_by; Q4 vendor_assignments.share_contact; Q21 closed status; Q3 call_request activity; Q12 CMS dormant; Q16 GST dormant; Q1 native apps need no table changes.

nodes.label: Entity index with phases and restricted fields (§19)
nodes.norm_label: entity index with phases and restricted fields (§19)
nodes.rationale: Lists every entity with module, phase (per SPEC §11 as adjusted by A-10) and the fields or whole tables the permission matrix guards server-side. Count: 108 tables including join tables, two dormant, against 35 rows in SPEC §4.

nodes.label: Module overview ER diagram (§2)
nodes.norm_label: module overview er diagram (§2)
nodes.rationale: Core entities only: leads convert to client_accounts, which hold subscriptions, service_agreements, saved_hotels, hotel_enquiries and wedding_projects; the wedding project is the parent of functions, budget lines, vendor assignments, designs, approvals, requests, family groups, room blocks, tasks, incidents, invoices and documents.

nodes.label: AMBIGUITY finding (AM)
nodes.norm_label: ambiguity finding (am)
nodes.rationale: A sentence that can be read two ways; the brief says which reading was taken. 15 in the audit, 9 placed; the other six are modelling detail answered in the data model.

nodes.label: ASSUMED placeholder (A/U/W/T/P)
nodes.norm_label: assumed placeholder (a/u/w/t/p)
nodes.rationale: What was done in the meantime, with its identifier. No price, fee or term is in code; every open policy is a tagged assumption so that design could continue.

nodes.label: COVERED requirement
nodes.norm_label: covered requirement
nodes.rationale: A requirement the design meets as written, marked so AMPM can see what needs no discussion.

nodes.label: GAP finding (GP)
nodes.norm_label: gap finding (gp)
nodes.rationale: Something the platform needs that no document specifies; each names its audit identifier and says how the design fills it meanwhile. 44 in the audit, 38 placed in the brief, 6 purely technical ones in the architecture plan.

nodes.label: AC-01 Public enquiry saves source and owner; team tracks follow-up
nodes.norm_label: ac-01 public enquiry saves source and owner; team tracks follow-up
nodes.rationale: Duplicate leads are flagged, never refused or auto-merged; a converted lead becomes read-only and the only path to an account is an invitation.

nodes.label: AC-02 Subscription activates hotel discovery without exposing full wedding modules
nodes.norm_label: ac-02 subscription activates hotel discovery without exposing full wedding modules
nodes.rationale: Online purchase, manual bank transfer and renewal all activate exactly the plan's modules; expiry removes modules and nothing else; the trial test AC-02.8 is dormant because the demo serves as the trial (Q3); no self-registration route exists.

nodes.label: AC-02.11 Renewal restores access and preserves data
nodes.norm_label: ac-02.11 renewal restores access and preserves data
nodes.rationale: Nothing is deleted on expiry, so a new subscription makes the six saved hotels and both enquiries reachable again with their history (Q3).

nodes.label: AC-03 Demo account cannot access records outside demo scope
nodes.norm_label: ac-03 demo account cannot access records outside demo scope
nodes.rationale: Demo data lives in the same database behind flags (V-10); rates are masked, non-demo hotels are 404, demo rows are invisible to operational staff and demo users cannot export.

nodes.label: AC-04 Hotel search shows freshness of pricing; unverified availability is never shown as confirmed
nodes.norm_label: ac-04 hotel search shows freshness of pricing; unverified availability is never shown as confirmed
nodes.rationale: Verified, stale and unverified cards carry distinct labels; the word 'confirmed' must not appear in rate context; availability is labelled separately from rates and answered inside an enquiry.

nodes.label: AC-05 AMPM records negotiation and site visit without exposing internal notes
nodes.norm_label: ac-05 ampm records negotiation and site visit without exposing internal notes
nodes.rationale: Internal-only events, restricted enquiry fields and hotel contacts never serialise to clients; 'preview as client' must be byte-identical to the real client response; an enquiry is not a confirmed booking until a done confirmed milestone and a signed contract exist; chargeable services wait for an active agreement.

nodes.label: AC-06 Engaged client receives correct project and permissions
nodes.norm_label: ac-06 engaged client receives correct project and permissions
nodes.rationale: Project creation needs only minimal fields and back-fills saved hotels, enquiry and agreement; client roles and the finance flag shape the portal with no placeholder for missing regions; membership removal ends access immediately; on-behalf decisions need evidence and a badge (V-14).

nodes.label: AC-07 Multiple functions have independent vendors, schedules, budgets and approvals
nodes.norm_label: ac-07 multiple functions have independent vendors, schedules, budgets and approvals
nodes.rationale: Approving one function's proposal leaves the other untouched; cancelling a function keeps its records (soft delete).

nodes.label: AC-08 Vendor shortlist permits fewer than five options; it does not require exactly ten
nodes.norm_label: ac-08 vendor shortlist permits fewer than five options; it does not require exactly ten
nodes.rationale: SPEC 1.2 says 'aiming for 5 to 10' but two options and twelve options must both present cleanly; availability conflicts warn but do not block.

nodes.label: AC-09 Approval refers to the exact design, menu or proposal version; revisions do not overwrite it
nodes.norm_label: ac-09 approval refers to the exact design, menu or proposal version; revisions do not overwrite it
nodes.rationale: A new version supersedes and the old one is immutable; approval locks the version and budget line; menu approval freezes the guaranteed headcount; approving an invitation does not send it.

nodes.label: AC-10 Self-service and AMPM-assisted RSVP update the same guest database without duplicates
nodes.norm_label: ac-10 self-service and ampm-assisted rsvp update the same guest database without duplicates
nodes.rationale: Both paths upsert the same guest_function_attendance rows and add rsvp_responses snapshots; per-side links identify the household (Q7); submitted responses are locked and corrections go through the RSVP team; allergies are sensitive; identity capture is conditional and audited.

nodes.label: AC-10.11 Side link: a guest identifies their household
nodes.norm_label: ac-10.11 side link: a guest identifies their household
nodes.rationale: An exact match opens the household's RSVP; a near match is held for RSVP-team review; no household data is shown before a confirmed match; a groom-side household cannot be found through the bride-side link (Q7).

nodes.label: AC-10.12 Unmatched guests are held for review
nodes.norm_label: ac-10.12 unmatched guests are held for review
nodes.rationale: A pending household with identification_status review counts for nothing until the RSVP team approves (Q7).

nodes.label: AC-10.13 Submitted responses are locked; corrections go through the team
nodes.norm_label: ac-10.13 submitted responses are locked; corrections go through the team
nodes.rationale: The reopened link shows a read-only summary; a correction request creates a guest_support_requests row and RG's change writes the same attendance rows with response_source ampm_call (Q7).

nodes.label: AC-11 Attendance changes update totals and flag downstream planning impacts
nodes.norm_label: ac-11 attendance changes update totals and flag downstream planning impacts
nodes.rationale: Recalculation changes expected_count but never guaranteed_count; rooming and transfer changes are flagged and logistics notified once; recalculation is idempotent.

nodes.label: AC-12 Unauthorised users cannot access restricted data by changing URLs, API requests or file links
nodes.norm_label: ac-12 unauthorised users cannot access restricted data by changing urls, api requests or file links
nodes.rationale: A generated suite covers every resource, principal and action; identifier tampering returns 404 with bodies and timing identical to a nonexistent id; signed file links expire and bind to one file; break-glass reads by SA are audited and alerted.

nodes.label: AC-13 Production readiness cannot be completed without required checks or an authorised exception
nodes.norm_label: ac-13 production readiness cannot be completed without required checks or an authorised exception
nodes.rationale: Readiness derives automatically from required items; exceptions may only be authorised by SA (Q10), PM and HL attempts return 403.

nodes.label: AC-14 Incidents can be assigned, escalated and closed with resolution notes
nodes.norm_label: ac-14 incidents can be assigned, escalated and closed with resolution notes
nodes.rationale: Critical incidents escalate automatically along the configured chain; critical resolution requires notes; client visibility is off by default and never exposes description or notes.

nodes.label: AC-15 Closure checks departure, lost-and-found, vendor completion and financial reconciliation
nodes.norm_label: ac-15 closure checks departure, lost-and-found, vendor completion and financial reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Each closure item verifies against data (409 until satisfied); closing deletes nothing; client access ends after the configured window and only SA may reopen; retention after closure requires SA approval (Q17).

nodes.label: AC-16 Responsive and accessible interfaces
nodes.norm_label: ac-16 responsive and accessible interfaces
nodes.rationale: Key screens render at 1280, 1024 and 375 px; WCAG 2.1 AA via axe-core; the guest wizard gets a manual keyboard and screen-reader pass.

nodes.label: AC-17 Secure authentication
nodes.norm_label: ac-17 secure authentication
nodes.rationale: Staff must enrol an authenticator before first use; clients and prospects sign in by mobile OTP (Q13); lockout with generic errors; single-use time-boxed tokens; Argon2id password storage; guest sessions bound to the household token.

nodes.label: AC-17.9 Mobile OTP sign-in for prospects and clients
nodes.norm_label: ac-17.9 mobile otp sign-in for prospects and clients
nodes.rationale: Codes are single use and expire in ten minutes; an uninvited number receives a neutral message and no session (Q13).

nodes.label: AC-18 Server-side validation on every protected request
nodes.norm_label: ac-18 server-side validation on every protected request
nodes.rationale: Validations are generated from field-matrix.csv; required-at-stage rules return 409; mass assignment of internal_cost, is_demo or status is never applied; uniqueness returns 409.

nodes.label: AC-19 Encryption in transit and at rest
nodes.norm_label: ac-19 encryption in transit and at rest
nodes.rationale: TLS 1.2+ with HSTS; three customer-managed keys with the restricted bucket on its own key; no secrets in code, images or logs.

nodes.label: AC-20 Private file storage, expiring links and safe uploads
nodes.norm_label: ac-20 private file storage, expiring links and safe uploads
nodes.rationale: Content-type detection, size limits, antivirus scan, image metadata stripping; document access follows the owning record's visibility.

nodes.label: AC-21 Audit trail
nodes.norm_label: ac-21 audit trail
nodes.rationale: Every listed action writes one event with actor, entity, before and after; audit_events is append-only at the database level and partitioned monthly; viewer scope follows roles.

nodes.label: AC-22 Backups and tested restoration
nodes.norm_label: ac-22 backups and tested restoration
nodes.rationale: Point-in-time restore drill within 4 hours and 15 minutes of data (RPO/RTO measured, not assumed, V-13); object storage restore from versions and replica region; backup failure alerts.

nodes.label: AC-24 Media optimisation and controlled video delivery
nodes.norm_label: ac-24 media optimisation and controlled video delivery
nodes.rationale: Derivatives generated by job; video transcoded and served only with expiring signed tokens; rights status gates client and public visibility.

nodes.label: AC-25 Configurable packages, categories, statuses and pricing
nodes.norm_label: ac-25 configurable packages, categories, statuses and pricing
nodes.rationale: Reference data edits take effect without a deploy; thresholds drive automation; a CI static check fails the build on any commercial literal in code (BIZ rule 8).

nodes.label: AC-26 Clear errors, duplicate-submission prevention and form recovery
nodes.norm_label: ac-26 clear errors, duplicate-submission prevention and form recovery
nodes.rationale: Double submission creates one record via idempotency keys; drafts survive refresh; errors name the field, keep input and are announced to assistive technology.

nodes.label: AC-27 Retention, deletion and privacy
nodes.norm_label: ac-27 retention, deletion and privacy
nodes.rationale: Consent is captured with its notice version; data principal export and erasure anonymise personal fields but keep attendance counts; retention deletes only after SA approval; logs contain no personal data.

nodes.label: AC-28 Integration boundaries
nodes.norm_label: ac-28 integration boundaries
nodes.rationale: Adapters are contract-tested against sandboxes; card data never leaves AMPM; provider outages retry with backoff and dead-letter; payloads carry only the fields listed in architecture section 10.

nodes.label: AC-29 Notifications and automation
nodes.norm_label: ac-29 notifications and automation
nodes.rationale: Approval requests go to CO and approvers with can_approve, never CV; material changes create review tasks; the notification log is complete; preferences and opt-in are honoured.

nodes.label: AC-30 Reports and exports
nodes.norm_label: ac-30 reports and exports
nodes.rationale: Every SPEC section 9 report computes from the seed; permissions follow permission-matrix section 5.16; the rooming list export for hotels carries names, dates and room category only.

nodes.label: AC-31 Status transitions and guards
nodes.norm_label: ac-31 status transitions and guards
nodes.rationale: Transition tests are generated from permission-matrix section 7: unlisted principals get 403, unlisted transitions get 409 with the guard message; status labels are display only.

nodes.label: AC-32 Entitlement resolution and downgrades
nodes.norm_label: ac-32 entitlement resolution and downgrades
nodes.rationale: Each account state yields exactly the documented module set; downgrade is read-only before removal; the entitlement cache is invalidated on write, not only on expiry.

nodes.label: AC-33 Offline behaviour on event day
nodes.norm_label: ac-33 offline behaviour on event day
nodes.rationale: Read caches with an 'offline since' indicator; queued mutations sync in order with original timestamps; server status wins conflicts and the offline change is logged; local data is encrypted and wiped on sign-out (first release on native builds, Q1).

nodes.label: AC-33.5 Local data is protected on native builds
nodes.norm_label: ac-33.5 local data is protected on native builds
nodes.rationale: The local store is encrypted at rest, holds only the user's role-scoped data and is wiped on sign-out (Q1).

nodes.label: AC-33.6 Offline state and pending changes are visible
nodes.norm_label: ac-33.6 offline state and pending changes are visible
nodes.rationale: An offline banner shows the pending-change count, which drains to zero on reconnect with each change keeping its original time (Q1).

nodes.label: AC-34 Performance and capacity
nodes.norm_label: ac-34 performance and capacity
nodes.rationale: k6 profiles for hotel search, RSVP burst, team workspace mixed load and job throughput; profiles rescaled to 200 hotels and 20 weddings (Q15).

nodes.label: AC-35 Imports
nodes.norm_label: ac-35 imports

nodes.label: AC-36 Finance integrity
nodes.norm_label: ac-36 finance integrity
nodes.rationale: Client and internal amounts never mix (schema assertion); approved amounts are locked except for an audited FA override; GST invoice tests AC-36.3 and AC-36.4 are dormant (Q16); refunds cannot exceed the original payment.

nodes.label: AC-37 Live chat alongside tracked requests
nodes.norm_label: ac-37 live chat alongside tracked requests

nodes.norm_label: ac-38 department-based access

nodes.label: Denial semantics: 404 for invisible records, 403 for forbidden actions, 400 for validation, 409 for transition guards
nodes.norm_label: denial semantics: 404 for invisible records, 403 for forbidden actions, 400 for validation, 409 for transition guards
nodes.rationale: A principal that may not see a record receives 404 with the same body as for a nonexistent record so existence cannot be inferred; a visible record with a forbidden action gets 403; validation failures return 400 naming the field; status-transition violations return 409 with the guard message. nodes.rationale: Primary specification (DOCX, 15 sections, 20 Oct 2026) generated with python-docx; no author, comments, tracked changes, revision history or sign-off, so its roles (§6), statuses (§7) and phases (§11) are treated as proposals until AMPM signs off (CF-7, RK-8).

nodes.label: TEAM-FLOW: AMPM App Visual Flowchart for team
nodes.norm_label: team-flow: ampm app visual flowchart for team
nodes.rationale: Level-1 navigation for the team app (A3 PDF, undated); five tabs Home, Clients, Weddings, Tasks, More and one straight line from qualified client to closure; footer says detailed section workflows are to be designed next.

nodes.label: Audit verdict: sufficient to start design under assumptions, not to build
nodes.norm_label: audit verdict: sufficient to start design under assumptions, not to build
nodes.rationale: SPEC is explicitly a starting specification and BIZ §9 and SPEC §13 leave commercial decisions open. Three problems stand out: the two flowcharts and the specification describe different products; the hotel database, the core of the subscription product, has no price field; and the commercial and access decisions that drive architecture (payment mode, one-time vs recurring, client-visible finance, native vs web, RSVP identity) are still open. Counts: 9 conflicts, 44 gaps, 15 ambiguities, 8 risks, 25 decisions for AMPM, 10 blocking design sign-off.

nodes.label: Concrete acceptance scenarios with tamper tests
nodes.norm_label: concrete acceptance scenarios with tamper tests
nodes.rationale: SPEC §12 gives concrete acceptance scenarios including tamper tests on URLs, API requests and file links.

nodes.label: Glossary and reconciled information architecture replacing the Level-1 flowcharts
nodes.norm_label: glossary and reconciled information architecture replacing the level-1 flowcharts
nodes.rationale: Both flowcharts are usable only as navigation sketches for the full-wedding-management case; the reconciled architecture must add the subscriber-only client-portal state, the Hotels and Guests areas of the team app and the branching sales funnel, with one agreed glossary before Level-2 flows are drawn.

nodes.label: Not everything mandatory; parallel workflows allowed
nodes.norm_label: not everything mandatory; parallel workflows allowed
nodes.rationale: BIZ rules 2 and 3 and SPEC §5 and §15: not all fields are compulsory and workflows may run in parallel.

nodes.label: Phasing with exit criteria
nodes.norm_label: phasing with exit criteria
nodes.rationale: SPEC §11 defines five delivery phases each with exit criteria; Phase 1's exit criterion is the lead-to-subscriber journey tested.

nodes.label: Three distinct service stages: discovery, optional consultancy, full management
nodes.norm_label: three distinct service stages: discovery, optional consultancy, full management
nodes.rationale: One stage never implies the next (the SPEC 'critical rule'); stated consistently in BIZ Step 5, WHY §1 and SPEC §1.2 and §15. Many clients stop at hotel discovery or consultancy and never get a wedding project, so the product must not be designed as a pure wedding-planning tool.

nodes.label: Principle: a wedding project is created when an agreement for anything beyond hotel help is accepted
nodes.norm_label: principle: a wedding project is created when an agreement for anything beyond hotel help is accepted
nodes.rationale: Follows business steps 5 and 6; confirmed.

nodes.label: Principle: five to ten vendor options is a guideline, never enforced
nodes.norm_label: principle: five to ten vendor options is a guideline, never enforced
nodes.rationale: The acceptance test says so; confirmed.

nodes.label: Principle: only a name, the account, tentative dates and a lead are required to create a wedding
nodes.norm_label: principle: only a name, the account, tentative dates and a lead are required to create a wedding
nodes.rationale: Rule 2, not everything mandatory; confirmed, and the client also enters couple, contact, dates and locations at activation.

nodes.label: artist_bookings
nodes.norm_label: artist_bookings
nodes.rationale: Performers, slots and riders. artist_name CLIENT; performance_type; slot_start/end; status enquiry/held/confirmed/performed/cancelled; technical_rider_document_id; hospitality_requirements; travel_arrangements; fee_internal RESTRICTED.

nodes.label: checklist_items
nodes.norm_label: checklist_items
nodes.rationale: item_key e.g. departures, lost_and_found, vendor_completion, final_accounts; is_required; status pending/done/not_applicable/exception; completed_by/at; exception_reason; exception_authorised_by (must hold the readiness-exception permission); evidence_document_id.

nodes.label: checklist_templates
nodes.norm_label: checklist_templates
nodes.rationale: template_key function_readiness / project_closure; entity_type function/project; items_json ordered items with is_required; is_active.

nodes.label: checklists
nodes.norm_label: checklists
nodes.rationale: Instantiated checklist. template_id; entity_type function/project with entity_id; status not_started/in_progress/blocked/complete/complete_with_exception. One per function (readiness) and one per project (closure).

nodes.label: client_feedback
nodes.norm_label: client_feedback
nodes.rationale: Post-wedding feedback (A-24, GP-29). submitted_by_user_id; overall_rating; comments_text; consent_to_publish; submitted_at.

nodes.label: function_programme_items
nodes.norm_label: function_programme_items
nodes.rationale: Shared programme the client and guests may see. start/end_time; title and description CLIENT; client_visible default true.

nodes.label: functions
nodes.norm_label: functions
nodes.rationale: Events within the wedding. function_type_id; name CLIENT; function_date; start/end_time; venue_kind hotel_venue/external_venue/tbd with two optional foreign keys hotel_venue_id and external_venue_id (AM-2); guest_estimate; theme and dress_code CLIENT; status planned/confirmed/cancelled and readiness_status not_started/in_progress/blocked/ready/live/completed derived from the checklist (A-26, AM-3); readiness_exception_note and readiness_exception_by for documented authorised exceptions (SPEC §7); internal_notes RESTRICTED.

nodes.label: incidents
nodes.norm_label: incidents
nodes.rationale: Event-day issues and escalation. function_id nullable; reported_by/at; severity low/medium/high/critical; category guest/vendor/venue/safety/transport/other; status open/assigned/in_progress/escalated/resolved/closed; assigned_user_id; escalated_to_user_id/escalated_at; resolution_notes required before resolved when severity is critical (SPEC §7); client_visible default false. Escalation rules (e.g. escalate to the project lead after 15 minutes unassigned) live in configurations.

nodes.label: Module F — Functions, programme and run-of-show
nodes.norm_label: module f — functions, programme and run-of-show
nodes.rationale: Covers SPEC §3 Functions (function, schedule, checklist, venue, run-of-show). Readiness checklist uses the generic checklist tables of module O. Resolves AM-2 (venue typing) and AM-3 (status versus readiness).

nodes.label: Module H — Vendors, artists and production
nodes.norm_label: module h — vendors, artists and production
nodes.rationale: Covers SPEC §3 Vendors and the artist, technical rider and production item records of Food/entertainment/production. Resolves GP-21 (vendor availability) and the vendor decision field of SPEC §5. Vendor portfolios are media_assets with owner_type = vendor.

nodes.label: Module M — Tasks, staffing and incidents
nodes.norm_label: module m — tasks, staffing and incidents
nodes.rationale: Covers SPEC §3 Tasks/risk (task, dependency, staff assignment, incident, resolution). Resolves GP-30 (staffing). Incident updates use the generic comments table of module I.

nodes.label: Module O — Checklists, closure and feedback
nodes.norm_label: module o — checklists, closure and feedback
nodes.rationale: Covers the checklist, readiness check and closure records of SPEC §3 and the feedback step in the team flowchart (GP-29). The same two tables serve function readiness and project closure.

nodes.label: production_items
nodes.norm_label: production_items
nodes.rationale: Sound, light, stage, tents and effects. category sound/lighting/stage/led/tent/props/sfx/power/other; description; quantity; status planned/ordered/delivered/installed/tested/struck; owner_user_id; checklist_item_id nullable links to a readiness item.

nodes.label: run_of_show_items
nodes.norm_label: run_of_show_items
nodes.rationale: Internal cue sheet. sequence; planned_start/end; cue; description; owner_user_id; vendor_assignment_id nullable; status pending/in_progress/done/skipped; actual_start/end; notes. Internal only (SPEC §2.4).

nodes.label: staff_assignments
nodes.norm_label: staff_assignments
nodes.rationale: On-site rosters (GP-30). function_id nullable; user_id; on_site_role function_lead/hospitality_desk/vendor_liaison/transport/floater; shift_start/end; status planned/confirmed/on_duty/off_duty/cancelled.

nodes.label: task_dependencies
nodes.norm_label: task_dependencies
nodes.rationale: task_id depends on depends_on_task_id; dependency_type finish_to_start.

nodes.label: tasks
nodes.norm_label: tasks
nodes.rationale: Accountability and milestones. project_id nullable (global tasks allowed); function_id nullable; owner_user_id; due_at; priority low/normal/high/urgent; status not_started/in_progress/blocked/completed/cancelled; is_milestone shown on the client dashboard; client_visible for pending decisions the client must act on; blocked_reason; related entity_type/entity_id; checklist_item_id nullable.

nodes.label: vendor_assignments
nodes.norm_label: vendor_assignments
nodes.rationale: Options, decisions and delivery per wedding. function_id nullable; vendor_id; category_id; scope_text CLIENT; status option/shortlisted/selected/contracted/delivering/completed/cancelled/declined; client_decision none/interested/shortlisted/selected/declined with client_decision_at/by (SPEC §5); presented_at (the client sees the option from here); contract_id nullable; completion_confirmed_at/by (vendor completion for closure); share_contact true only in an AMPM-approved case (Q4); internal_notes RESTRICTED. Five to ten options per category is a guideline, not a constraint.

nodes.label: vendor_availability
nodes.norm_label: vendor_availability
nodes.rationale: Verified availability windows (GP-21). date_from/to; status available/tentative/booked/unavailable; verified_at/verified_by; source; note.

nodes.label: vendor_categories
nodes.norm_label: vendor_categories
nodes.rationale: Reference table. category_key: decor, photography, videography, sound_light, artists, catering, tents_props, sfx, transport, other; parent_id; is_active.

nodes.label: vendor_category_links
nodes.norm_label: vendor_category_links
nodes.rationale: Join table vendor_id x category_id for additional categories a vendor offers.

nodes.label: vendor_deliverables
nodes.norm_label: vendor_deliverables
nodes.rationale: Delivery tracking and acceptance. function_id nullable; title; due_at; status pending/in_progress/delivered/accepted/rejected; accepted_by/accepted_at. completion_confirmed_at on the assignment is set when all deliverables are accepted.

nodes.label: vendor_proposals
nodes.norm_label: vendor_proposals
nodes.rationale: Versioned proposals AMPM shows the client. version_number; title, description_client and inclusions_text CLIENT; client_visible_amount CLIENT and internal_cost RESTRICTED (A-4); status draft/shared/revision_requested/accepted/declined/superseded; shared_at; decided_at/decided_by_user_id; approval_id points at the approval that locked that exact version; document_id; supersedes_proposal_id.

nodes.label: vendor_quotes
nodes.norm_label: vendor_quotes
nodes.rationale: Raw quotes sent by vendors to AMPM, RESTRICTED table. vendor_id; project_id; vendor_assignment_id nullable; version_number; amount; received_at; valid_until; document_id; status received/shortlisted/selected/rejected/expired; internal_notes.

nodes.label: vendors
nodes.norm_label: vendors
nodes.rationale: Vendor master. name CLIENT when presented; primary_category_id; description_client CLIENT; contact_name, phone and email RESTRICTED (clients deal with vendors through AMPM, BIZ §2.C); website; instagram_handle; base_city; service_area; status prospective/active/preferred/inactive/blacklisted; internal_rating and internal_notes RESTRICTED; gstin; bank_details_document_id RESTRICTED; onboarded_at. Vendors never log in (A-22).

nodes.label: Dashboards are queries, not tables
nodes.norm_label: dashboards are queries, not tables
nodes.rationale: Overdue tasks, unconfirmed vendors, unpaid milestones and incomplete readiness checks are dashboard queries over existing tables (SPEC §8); compare-hotels is a view over saved_hotels; variance and manifests are reports; no extra tables are needed.

nodes.label: Function workspace is a filtered view
nodes.norm_label: function workspace is a filtered view
nodes.rationale: Budget lines, vendor assignments, menus, design items, tasks, incidents and production items all reference functions.id optionally, so a function's workspace is a filtered view of those tables rather than a separate structure.

nodes.label: Material change requests raise impact flags
nodes.norm_label: material change requests raise impact flags
nodes.rationale: A material client request (A-25) sets is_material and populates impact_flags_json, raising flags on budgets, contracts, tasks and run-of-show items as SPEC §8 requires; thresholds such as material_change_threshold_pct live in configurations.

nodes.label: Quotes are internal, proposals are client-facing
nodes.norm_label: quotes are internal, proposals are client-facing
nodes.rationale: vendor_quotes are what vendors send AMPM and are internal. vendor_proposals are what AMPM shows the client, versioned, with a client amount and an internal cost (A-4). A proposal's approval_id points at the approval that locked that exact version.

nodes.label: Readiness status derived from the checklist
nodes.norm_label: readiness status derived from the checklist
nodes.rationale: functions.readiness_status is recalculated whenever a checklist_items row changes: ready when every required item is done or exception; blocked when any item is flagged blocked by its owner; live and completed are set by the project manager on the day. A function cannot reach ready until every is_required item is done or carries an exception authorised by a user holding the readiness-exception permission (SPEC §7).

nodes.label: Two schedules on purpose: programme versus run-of-show
nodes.norm_label: two schedules on purpose: programme versus run-of-show
nodes.rationale: function_programme_items is the shared programme the client and guests may see (SPEC §2.3 shared schedules); run_of_show_items is the internal cue sheet with owners, vendors and actual times (SPEC §2.4).

nodes.label: Vendor contact details restricted
nodes.norm_label: vendor contact details restricted
nodes.rationale: Vendor contact details are restricted because clients deal with vendors through AMPM (BIZ §2.C). If AMPM wants selected vendors' contacts shared after selection, vendor_assignments.share_contact allows it per assignment in an AMPM-approved case (Q4, Q22; open question §21.2).

nodes.label: Vendor options presented to the client
nodes.norm_label: vendor options presented to the client
nodes.rationale: Presenting a vendor creates a vendor_assignments row with status = option and presented_at set. Five to ten options per category is a guideline, not a constraint (SPEC §12). The client_decision field (none/interested/shortlisted/selected/declined) records the family's response.

nodes.label: AM-12: invitations are design work (Phase 2) and distribution work (Phase 3)
nodes.norm_label: am-12: invitations are design work (phase 2) and distribution work (phase 3)

nodes.label: AM-14: 'a paid business asset' could hint at licensing to other planners
nodes.norm_label: am-14: 'a paid business asset' could hint at licensing to other planners

nodes.label: AM-8: 'three distinct environments' - three hosted systems or three experiences of one
nodes.norm_label: am-8: 'three distinct environments' - three hosted systems or three experiences of one

nodes.label: AMPM business process (Steps 1-10)
nodes.norm_label: ampm business process (steps 1-10)
nodes.rationale: Enquiry, introduction and demo, optional subscription, hotel exploration, optional hotel services, project creation if hired, parallel activities, vendor options, execution, closure.

nodes.label: CF-1: the demo belongs to neither the four experiences nor the three environments, and to no phase
nodes.norm_label: cf-1: the demo belongs to neither the four experiences nor the three environments, and to no phase

nodes.label: CF-4: team-app flowchart starts at a qualified client, omitting demo, subscription and hotel work
nodes.norm_label: cf-4: team-app flowchart starts at a qualified client, omitting demo, subscription and hotel work

nodes.label: CF-5: AMPM creates every account (Why note) versus a payment journey from the website (specification)
nodes.norm_label: cf-5: ampm creates every account (why note) versus a payment journey from the website (specification)

nodes.label: CF-9: three distinct environments (Why note) versus one shared backend (specification)
nodes.norm_label: cf-9: three distinct environments (why note) versus one shared backend (specification)

nodes.label: Customer journey stages 1-5 (website, demo, subscription, project, full access)
nodes.norm_label: customer journey stages 1-5 (website, demo, subscription, project, full access)
nodes.rationale: Seeing AMPM, trying a demo, buying a subscription and receiving full project access are four different stages; the design has a client account state for each.

nodes.label: GP-1: no definition of what each account state may see
nodes.norm_label: gp-1: no definition of what each account state may see

nodes.label: GP-2: demo undefined (how granted, what it shows, when it ends) and no trial status
nodes.norm_label: gp-2: demo undefined (how granted, what it shows, when it ends) and no trial status

nodes.label: GP-27: attaching pre-project saved hotels and enquiries to a new project not specified
nodes.norm_label: gp-27: attaching pre-project saved hotels and enquiries to a new project not specified

nodes.label: GP-5: no path from a hotel-help request to agreed, possibly paid, work
nodes.norm_label: gp-5: no path from a hotel-help request to agreed, possibly paid, work

nodes.label: Five implementation phases (foundation, planning, guest operations, live execution, stabilisation)
nodes.norm_label: five implementation phases (foundation, planning, guest operations, live execution, stabilisation)
nodes.rationale: Demo and trial placed in Phase 1 (A-10); Phase 1 assumed to include the full hotel-assistance workflow, online payment and website editing (Q10); invitation design in Phase 2 and sending in Phase 3 (AM-12); each phase has a named test pack.

nodes.label: Q10: first-release scope and phase contents
nodes.norm_label: q10: first-release scope and phase contents

nodes.label: Q2: payment path - AMPM creates the account, client pays in the portal
nodes.norm_label: q2: payment path - ampm creates the account, client pays in the portal

nodes.label: Sample Jaipur wedding (four functions, 412 guests)
nodes.norm_label: sample jaipur wedding (four functions, 412 guests)
nodes.rationale: The brief's worked example (250 guests in Jaipur) is the sample wedding used throughout the drafts and the test data, so every screen and test is checked against the case AMPM described.

nodes.label: Three distinct environments (public website, demo/trial, private platform)
nodes.norm_label: three distinct environments (public website, demo/trial, private platform)
nodes.rationale: CF-9/AM-8: could mean three separately hosted systems or three experiences of one; the specification asks for one shared backend, so one platform was built with flagged demo accounts and demo weddings.

nodes.label: Customer journey as described in the Why AMPM App note (Stages 1-5)
nodes.norm_label: customer journey as described in the why ampm app note (stages 1-5)

nodes.label: Decision gate: engages AMPM beyond hotels?
nodes.norm_label: decision gate: engages ampm beyond hotels?
nodes.rationale: Makes the critical rule visible: no leads to remaining a subscriber, yes to a service agreement and wedding record.

nodes.label: Why AMPM App note
nodes.norm_label: why ampm app note
nodes.rationale: Positions AMPM as a paid, client-based platform rather than a public app: four stages (see, demo, subscribe, full project), three environments, a private hotel database and access-control rules including no self-registration.

nodes.label: Client account states (subscriber-only, engaged, expired, closed)
nodes.norm_label: client account states (subscriber-only, engaged, expired, closed)
nodes.rationale: GP-1: three sources of access (subscription, agreement, project) were named without saying how they combine. The permission matrix has a table per state: an expired subscriber keeps saved-hotel names and read access to enquiries, an engaged client keeps the wedding workspace whatever the subscription does, and expiry never deletes anything.

nodes.label: Critical rule: hotel-discovery subscription never implies full wedding management
nodes.norm_label: critical rule: hotel-discovery subscription never implies full wedding management
nodes.rationale: A subscription grants only hotel modules; wedding modules come only from a service agreement and project membership. Subscription and service agreement are two separate records so the service stages stay distinct but connected.

nodes.label: Demo / trial mode
nodes.norm_label: demo / trial mode
nodes.rationale: The Why note requires a distinct demo environment that the specification mentions only as one screen and one test and assigns to no phase (CF-1, GP-2). Placed in Phase 1 as a mode of one platform: Sales grants it from the lead record, it is time-boxed, shows a curated set of hotels with prices hidden plus one sample wedding, and every query for a demo user is limited to flagged records (U-1, A-10, A-28). A separately hosted demo is possible at extra cost.

nodes.label: Built for AMPM alone, not for licensing to other planners
nodes.norm_label: built for ampm alone, not for licensing to other planners
nodes.rationale: AM-14: 'a paid business asset' could hint at licensing the software to other planners; one structural change is cheaper now than later if that is a real intention (A-30).

nodes.label: Service agreement for hotel assistance and wedding management
nodes.norm_label: service agreement for hotel assistance and wedding management
nodes.rationale: GP-5: an availability check is included in the subscription; negotiation, site visits, contract review and booking assistance wait for an agreement the team sends and the client accepts in the portal (U-3). An accepted agreement for anything beyond hotel help creates the wedding project (U-6).

nodes.label: Subscription purchase path: request on website, AMPM invites, client pays in portal, modules activate
nodes.norm_label: subscription purchase path: request on website, ampm invites, client pays in portal, modules activate
nodes.rationale: CF-5: the Why note says AMPM creates every account and nobody registers, the specification describes a website payment journey. Reconciled: the client requests access on the website, AMPM creates the account and invites them, the client pays inside the portal online or by bank transfer (U-2, W-15). No registration route exists, with a test.

nodes.label: Wedding project
nodes.norm_label: wedding project
nodes.rationale: U-6: created when an agreement beyond hotel help is accepted; links the account's saved hotels and enquiries automatically (GP-27); only a name, the account, tentative dates and a lead are required at creation, so nothing is re-entered and no giant mandatory form exists.

nodes.label: Create wedding record from an accepted service agreement (unique ID, scope, staff and client members)
nodes.norm_label: create wedding record from an accepted service agreement (unique id, scope, staff and client members)
nodes.rationale: Triggered by an accepted service agreement for anything beyond hotel help (U-6, Q10; user flows Flow 3).

nodes.label: Upgraded customer journey
nodes.norm_label: upgraded customer journey
nodes.rationale: Inserts hotel discovery and assistance and an engage decision between subscription and project, keeps non-engaging clients as subscribers with nothing deleted, and ends with closure.

nodes.label: Demo or trial stage: granted by Sales, time-boxed, sample data, expires
nodes.norm_label: demo or trial stage: granted by sales, time-boxed, sample data, expires
nodes.rationale: A stage the Why note requires but no other document specified (GP-2, CF-1; user flows Flow 1, U-1).

nodes.label: Hotel discovery and assistance branch for the subscriber
nodes.norm_label: hotel discovery and assistance branch for the subscriber
nodes.rationale: The branch most clients take and the flowchart omitted (CF-4; user flows Flow 2); availability checks included, other services by agreement (GP-5, U-3).

nodes.label: Stays a subscriber: renew, or expire to read-only, nothing deleted
nodes.norm_label: stays a subscriber: renew, or expire to read-only, nothing deleted
nodes.rationale: GP-1; user flows Flow 12.

nodes.label: Subscription stage: AMPM invites, client pays in the portal, modules activate
nodes.norm_label: subscription stage: ampm invites, client pays in the portal, modules activate
nodes.rationale: Purchase path defined (CF-5, Q2; user flows Flow 1, U-2).

nodes.label: CP-10 Hotel proposal detail and decision
nodes.norm_label: cp-10 hotel proposal detail and decision
nodes.rationale: Review a negotiated offer and Accept, Request revision or Decline against the exact shared version (SPEC 12 version lock); internal amounts absent; expired validity disables the decision; a staff-recorded decision shows the Recorded on behalf badge (P-9).

nodes.label: CP-22 Functions list
nodes.norm_label: cp-22 functions list
nodes.rationale: Readiness status and internal notes absent; cancelled functions shown struck through.

nodes.label: CP-23 Function workspace
nodes.norm_label: cp-23 function workspace
nodes.rationale: One function's shared plan; run-of-show, production items, artist fees and staffing are absent.

nodes.label: CP-26 Vendor options
nodes.norm_label: cp-26 vendor options
nodes.rationale: Board per category (Presented, Shortlisted, Selected, Declined). Vendor contact details, raw quotes, internal rating and notes absent; fewer than five options is normal and not labelled incomplete (SPEC 12).

nodes.label: CP-27 Vendor proposal detail
nodes.norm_label: cp-27 vendor proposal detail
nodes.rationale: Approve, revise or decline a vendor proposal version; internal_cost absent; approved versions read-only; may await a second approver (1 of 2 decisions).

nodes.label: CP-28 Design studio
nodes.norm_label: cp-28 design studio

nodes.label: CP-29 Design item detail
nodes.norm_label: cp-29 design item detail
nodes.rationale: Review a version with pinned comments (annotation_json) and decide; internal comments and the brief are absent (A-20); drafts not yet shared are unreachable.

nodes.label: CP-30 Invitations and save-the-dates
nodes.norm_label: cp-30 invitations and save-the-dates
nodes.rationale: Approve invitation designs and watch distribution counts by channel; recipient-level delivery detail stays with the RSVP team in TW-41.

nodes.label: CP-33 RSVP progress
nodes.norm_label: cp-33 rsvp progress
nodes.rationale: Counts per function and side; Viewers see numbers only, never names (permission-matrix 6).

nodes.label: CP-34 Menus
nodes.norm_label: cp-34 menus
nodes.rationale: Approve menus per function; per-category headcounts and caterer guarantees are internal (data-model 14).

nodes.label: CP-35 Approvals inbox
nodes.norm_label: cp-35 approvals inbox
nodes.rationale: Every decision waiting for the client in one place (PORTAL-FLOW Approvals); after Q5 either representative may approve.

nodes.label: CP-36 Requests
nodes.norm_label: cp-36 requests
nodes.rationale: Questions, change requests and support in one typed, tracked place instead of chat (W-8, A-20, A-21). A change request to an approved item leads to a new version and a new approval, never an edit of the approved one (flow 6).

nodes.label: CP-37 Request detail
nodes.norm_label: cp-37 request detail
nodes.rationale: Thread and outcome of one request; staff internal comments never appear; impact_flags_json and budget_impact_amount are summarised in plain language, not exposed raw.

nodes.label: CP-42 Live chat
nodes.norm_label: cp-42 live chat
nodes.rationale: Added for AMPM's Q20 decision: immediate help from AMPM, distinct from tracked requests. A conversation never carries an approval or a budget figure; anything formal becomes a request via Turn this into a request. Conversations are scoped to the account and wedding; when no staff are online the composer says replies come by the preferred channel.

nodes.label: Client portal: engaged wedding CP-20 to CP-42 (Phases 2 to 4)
nodes.norm_label: client portal: engaged wedding cp-20 to cp-42 (phases 2 to 4)
nodes.rationale: Unlocked when a service agreement is accepted and a project created: dashboard, overview, functions, budget, vendors, designs, invitations, guests, menus, approvals, requests, documents, notifications, feedback, closed state, live chat.

nodes.label: T5 Approval detail template
nodes.norm_label: t5 approval detail template
nodes.rationale: Record header with version timeline on the left, preview or line items centre, approval panel and comment thread on the right. Used for proposals, designs, menus, invitations and budget approvals.

nodes.label: T7 Thread and timeline template
nodes.norm_label: t7 thread and timeline template
nodes.rationale: Chronological events and comments with filters (all, internal, client-visible) and a composer at the bottom.

nodes.label: TW-28 Hotel proposal editor
nodes.norm_label: tw-28 hotel proposal editor
nodes.rationale: Separate client and internal totals (A-4): client total computed from visible lines, internal panel (internal total, commission basis, margin) RESTRICTED-FINANCE and never shown in Preview as client; shared versions immutable.

nodes.label: TW-38 Vendor assignments for a project
nodes.norm_label: tw-38 vendor assignments for a project
nodes.rationale: Present options with an availability check for the function dates; record client decisions on behalf with evidence (P-9); fewer than five options never blocks presenting (SPEC 12).

nodes.label: TW-39 Vendor proposal editor
nodes.norm_label: tw-39 vendor proposal editor
nodes.rationale: Client and internal amounts separated (A-4); internal panel with internal cost, margin and linked raw quotes RESTRICTED-FINANCE; shared versions immutable; Preview as client renders CP-27.

nodes.label: TW-40 Design items and versions
nodes.norm_label: tw-40 design items and versions
nodes.rationale: Internal review thread defaults to internal; clients see only shared versions and client-visible items (A-20).

nodes.label: Append-only, monthly partitioned audit
nodes.norm_label: append-only, monthly partitioned audit
nodes.rationale: audit_events records every create, update, delete, approval, share, export and restricted-field read on the entities in permission matrix §9. Rows are append-only and partitioned by month (A-15). audit_events.project_id is denormalised so a project manager can read their own project's history without scanning everything. Open question §21.6: restricted-field reads audited for identity documents and internal cost; auditing every restricted read is possible but noisy.

nodes.label: Demo isolation at the repository layer
nodes.norm_label: demo isolation at the repository layer
nodes.rationale: Queries for a demo user are scoped to is_demo = true accounts and projects and demo_visible = true hotels at the repository layer, not in the interface (A-28). Open question §21.5: demo could use invented sample hotels seeded as inactive hotels with demo_visible = true.

nodes.label: Statuses fixed in code, labels configurable
nodes.norm_label: statuses fixed in code, labels configurable

nodes.label: Identity documents in a restricted bucket
nodes.norm_label: identity documents in a restricted bucket
nodes.rationale: A-8: identity documents live in a separate restricted bucket with its own key, are never included in exports, and every read writes an audit_events row with action = restricted_read. A retention job deletes the file and nulls file_document_id after retention_until, which after Q17 is set only when AMPM approves deletion.

nodes.label: Media rights gate visibility (GP-20)
nodes.norm_label: media rights gate visibility (gp-20)
nodes.rationale: Only rights_status = owned, licensed or consent_obtained may be set to client, demo or public visibility; the API rejects the rest.

nodes.label: Offline change queue mirrored by audit events
nodes.norm_label: offline change queue mirrored by audit events
nodes.rationale: Q1 native apps with offline use require no table changes; an offline change queue is a client-side store, mirrored by audit_events on sync (architecture §0a).

nodes.label: Offline decisions recorded on behalf of the client
nodes.norm_label: offline decisions recorded on behalf of the client
nodes.rationale: When the family approves on a call, staff record the decision with recorded_on_behalf_by and attach evidence_document_id; the audit log shows it was not the client's own click.

nodes.label: Polymorphic references limited to six tables
nodes.norm_label: polymorphic references limited to six tables
nodes.rationale: owner_type+owner_id, entity_type+entity_id and record_type+record_id are used only for documents, media, comments, approvals, audit events and notifications, each with a check constraint on the allowed types. Open question §21.4 keeps one polymorphic comments table rather than per-entity tables (cleaner indexing versus multiplied code).

nodes.norm_label: previous wedding media require consent (gp-20)
nodes.rationale: Previous wedding media are media_assets with owner_type = hotel, rights_status = consent_obtained and consent_source_project_id set; the permission matrix publishing rule refuses client or public visibility without it. hotel_wedding_references carry a consent_document_id from the referenced client.

nodes.norm_label: standard columns and soft delete
nodes.rationale: created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by, deleted_at on every table. Wedding, guest and finance records are never hard-deleted; physical deletion happens only through retention jobs (A-17), which after Q17 produce proposals awaiting AMPM approval.

nodes.norm_label: utc storage with per-project timezone
nodes.rationale: All timestamps are stored in UTC; wedding_projects.timezone (default Asia/Kolkata) drives display (A-16, AM-13).

nodes.norm_label: uuid v7 primary keys and fk naming
nodes.rationale: Every table has id UUID v7 (time-ordered). Foreign keys are named <table_singular>_id. Human-readable codes such as the wedding code AMPM-2027-014 are separate unique columns, never primary keys.

nodes.label: Visibility follows the owning record
nodes.norm_label: visibility follows the owning record
nodes.rationale: documents.visibility and media_assets.visibility are enumerations (internal, client, guest, public, demo). Everything else follows the owning record: a file attached to a vendor proposal is client-visible only if the proposal is shared and the user is a member of that project. The API enforces this on every request and every export (SPEC §6.1, §9).

nodes.label: RESTRICTED / SENSITIVE / CLIENT field markers
nodes.norm_label: restricted / sensitive / client field markers
nodes.rationale: RESTRICTED: internal only, server-side guarded. SENSITIVE: guest health or identity data. CLIENT: client-visible when the owning record is shared. Unmarked fields are internal by default and become client-visible only through the permission matrix rules.

nodes.label: MemPalace global hooks caveat (wing_api overwrite)
nodes.norm_label: mempalace global hooks caveat (wing_api overwrite)
nodes.rationale: MemPalace's own global hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json (mempal_save_hook.sh and mempal_precompact_hook.sh) file a running session's transcript under the shared wing wing_api without naming the project; because MemPalace keys drawers by content and upserts, they overwrite the wing the project hooks set. The global session-end hook is project-aware, so a cleanly ended session does end up in ampm. Fix: point the two global hooks at the project-aware runner (mempalace hook run --hook stop --harness claude-code, and --hook precompact) and re-key what is already in the shared wing with mempalace wings split --wing wing_api (plan first, then --yes).

nodes.rationale: Managed PostgreSQL, object storage, queues and containers; infrastructure as code; nothing hand-built on a server.

nodes.label: Principle: modular monolith, not microservices
nodes.norm_label: principle: modular monolith, not microservices
nodes.rationale: At T-7 scale one deployable API and one worker are simpler, cheaper and easier for a small team; module boundaries follow the data model so a later split is a deployment change, not a rewrite.

nodes.label: Principle: everything important is versioned, audited and recoverable
nodes.norm_label: principle: everything important is versioned, audited and recoverable
nodes.rationale: Soft deletes, immutable shared versions, append-only audit events, point-in-time recovery.

nodes.label: T-10 Full production topology from Phase 1
nodes.norm_label: t-10 full production topology from phase 1
nodes.rationale: No throwaway hosting; a reduced Phase 1 could run single-AZ on the same code.

nodes.label: T-11 Offline-first behaviour with sync and conflict log
nodes.norm_label: t-11 offline-first behaviour with sync and conflict log
nodes.rationale: Originally Phase 4 service-worker caching; changed to offline-first native apps from launch with sync, conflict detection and protected local storage.

nodes.label: T-12 Proposed service-level targets
nodes.norm_label: t-12 proposed service-level targets
nodes.rationale: 99.5 percent monthly availability, API p95 under 400 ms, pages interactive under 3 s on 4G, WCAG 2.1 AA; still open.

nodes.label: T-13 Backups: 35-day PITR, cross-region copies, RPO 15 min, RTO 4 h
nodes.norm_label: t-13 backups: 35-day pitr, cross-region copies, rpo 15 min, rto 4 h
nodes.rationale: Tighter targets need a warm standby in the second region at roughly double the database cost.

nodes.label: T-14 On-call cover on wedding days and deployment freeze while live
nodes.norm_label: t-14 on-call cover on wedding days and deployment freeze while live

nodes.label: T-1 Platform form factor: native iOS and Android apps plus static web
nodes.norm_label: t-1 platform form factor: native ios and android apps plus static web
nodes.rationale: Originally one responsive TypeScript web platform with PWA offline in Phase 4; AMPM changed to native team and client apps from one React Native (Expo) codebase, offline-first, with the public website on Next.js. Front-end effort roughly doubles; the backend is unchanged.

nodes.label: T-2 AWS Mumbai (ap-south-1) with Hyderabad backup copies
nodes.norm_label: t-2 aws mumbai (ap-south-1) with hyderabad backup copies
nodes.rationale: All personal data stays in India; containers and PostgreSQL keep the platform portable to Google Cloud or Azure India regions. Still open with AMPM.

nodes.label: T-5 Built-in content tables (dropped)
nodes.norm_label: t-5 built-in content tables (dropped)
nodes.rationale: AMPM decided there is no content editor; the website is static and maintained outside the app, so the cms_* tables are not built.

nodes.label: T-7 Sizing: modular monolith for about 200 hotels and 20 concurrent weddings
nodes.norm_label: t-7 sizing: modular monolith for about 200 hotels and 20 concurrent weddings
nodes.rationale: One API and one worker serve this with room for tenfold growth by adding replicas; module boundaries are the seams for a later split.

nodes.norm_label: u-7 offline operation during execution

nodes.label: Why AMPM App
nodes.norm_label: why ampm app
nodes.rationale: Argues that AMPM is a private, paid, client-based wedding management platform with a public marketing website and a controlled demo-to-client funnel, not a public app with open registration; this protects the proprietary hotel database and makes the software a paid business asset rather than a free public tool.

nodes.label: Critical Rule — Hotel-Discovery Subscription Does Not Automatically Activate Full Wedding Management
nodes.norm_label: critical rule — hotel-discovery subscription does not automatically activate full wedding management
nodes.rationale: Clients may select only the services they want; hotel discovery, optional hotel consultancy and complete wedding management are distinct but connected service stages.

nodes.label: Core Business Rule — Hotel Discovery and Complete Wedding Management Are Two Separate Services
nodes.norm_label: core business rule — hotel discovery and complete wedding management are two separate services
nodes.rationale: A client can purchase hotel discovery without appointing AMPM; discovery does not unlock vendor selection or wedding management; full planning access only after mutual agreement; AMPM decides the management fee separately (never calculated or displayed in the subscription); all internal costs, margins, vendor quotations and negotiation details remain private.

nodes.label: Access-Control Rules to Implement from the Beginning
nodes.norm_label: access-control rules to implement from the beginning
nodes.rationale: No public self-registration; AMPM admins create/approve accounts; module entitlements per subscription; subscription and wedding engagement tracked separately; full project access only after commercial approval and onboarding; per-wedding isolation; demo data separate; expiry/cancellation/upgrade without deleting wedding records.

nodes.label: Hotel Database as a Private AMPM Resource (not a public directory)
nodes.norm_label: hotel database as a private ampm resource (not a public directory)
nodes.rationale: Public visitors see only selected examples or previews; prospects see sample data in the demo; authorised subscribers access the module per plan; selections connect to the wedding once a project exists.

nodes.label: AMPM as a Private, Paid, Client-Based Platform
nodes.norm_label: ampm as a private, paid, client-based platform
nodes.rationale: Seeing AMPM, trying a limited demo, purchasing a subscription and receiving full wedding-project access are four different stages; the public website exists to attract, explain, demonstrate value and convert prospects into paying customers.

nodes.label: App Subscription Is Not the Complete Wedding Planning Service
nodes.norm_label: app subscription is not the complete wedding planning service
nodes.rationale: Paying for an app subscription does not automatically mean a client has purchased AMPM's complete wedding planning and execution service; these are separate commercial offerings even if they work together.

nodes.label: Three Distinct Environments (public website, demo/trial environment, private AMPM platform)
nodes.norm_label: three distinct environments (public website, demo/trial environment, private ampm platform)
nodes.rationale: The system should have three distinct environments, not one public app with open registration.
